source_notes.paraphrase: White Beryl Chapter 26 and illustrated manuscript Plate14 number thirty computational charts consecutively without a Chinese/Tibetan break. The introductory White Beryl allocation and Moonbeams present different 15-Chinese/15-Tibetan partitions. These are conflicting editorial taxonomies, not independent empirical astrological systems.

source_notes.paraphrase: White Beryl describes fifteen Chinese-chart starting animal pairs beginning Mouse/Ox identity, Tiger/Hare son, Dragon/Snake friend, Horse/Sheep enemy and Bird/Monkey mother relations, then cycles through other pairs; Tibetan starting-point groups are separately specified.

source_notes.paraphrase: The source counts anticlockwise from the female member of a starting year-sign pair for a subject born under a feminine-polarity year; clockwise from the male member of the pair for a masculine-polarity year. Year polarity must not be replaced with the person's sex.

source_notes.paraphrase: Each chart assesses eight ordered comparisons: log-men with vitality four backward; log-men with body four forward; log-men with destiny eleven backward; log-men with luck eleven forward; natal vitality with vitality seven backward; natal body with body seven forward; log-men with destiny at its own sector; log-men with luck at its own sector.

source_notes.paraphrase: For the thirty-chart calculation, mother relation gives three white markers, friend two white, identity Earth/Water one white, son one white and one black, identity Fire/Iron/Wood one black, enemy two black. These are category encodings, not observed occurrence counts.

source_notes.paraphrase: Thirty named charts multiplied by eight basic comparisons each gives 240 base pebbles in the elaborate procedure. The text also acknowledges moderate and concise variants, which cannot be assumed to share all 240 markers.

source_notes.paraphrase: An exemplary royal chart for a Fire Dragon subject begins from Fire Mouse and proceeds clockwise because of a male-polarity natal year; its eight worked elemental contrasts are illustrated as colored pebbles. This verifies source procedure, not the king's outcomes.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 1–7 in chapter order separately address kings/potentates, spiritual friends, mantrins, Bon priests, dignitaries/elders, adult men, and women/wives. This is a role-conditioned divination taxonomy, not seven universal birth traits.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 8–12 address children, young girls, servants/retainers, riding animals such as horses/mules, and cleft-hoofed animals such as yaks and sheep. Several subjects are nonhuman or property, so no uniform personality-scoring framework follows from the chart inventory.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 13–17 separately address compatible spouses, bridal departure timing, household/land, estate quality and metal household artefacts. These categories overlap source families already studied but are not independent confirmations of marriage/electional outcomes.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 18–21 cover childbirth, temple pollution, malevolent demon interpretations and good luck of elderly subjects, respectively. The source includes both potentially observable and doctrinally supernatural target claims.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 22–26 address duration of illness, death/funeral preparations, modes of corpse disposal, tomb qualities and ritual charms; these are post-event or high-stakes religious categories rather than legitimate individual medical predictions.

source_notes.paraphrase: Charts 27–30 address male vitality, young children's body element, women's destiny element, and luck of important/educated people. The target personal force and subject category must be bound before selecting one of these rules.

source_notes.paraphrase: The book adds general rules for groups of lower, central and upper pebbles: color composition changes its alleged reading for later life, present property and kinship. They require the chart-specific source assignment and are not standalone personality test observations.

methodological_warnings: Chapter 26 1–30 indexing and two Chinese/Tibetan 15/15 schemes are not the same partition.
Both an illustrative 8-sector computation and distinct consulted-source verbal predictions exist; no human accuracy measurements.
Source names certain nonhuman property, animal and spirit targets; do not reinterpret as survey traits.
Year polarity changes count direction and is independent of subject sex.
Some moral/cultural assertions and dangers are not medical, legal, cultural or ritual advice.
Original Tibetan and rare 'Phrul-gyi mig-tshags' remain unread.
